A.explanation: Circular anticlockwise loops do not represent an electrostatic field. Field lines must start on the positive charge and go radially outward.

B.explanation: Circular clockwise loops are incorrect for the same reason. A static point charge cannot produce closed loops.

C.explanation: Straight lines directed radially away from the $+$ charge correctly show repulsion of a positive test charge in all directions.

D.explanation: Straight radial lines pointing inward toward the $+$ charge describe a negative point charge, not a positive one.

hints: Look at the centre $+$ symbol and check whether the arrows in each diagram point toward the charge, away from it, or around it.
Recall that electric field direction is the direction of force on a small positive test charge placed in the field.
Compare radial straight lines with circular closed loops - only one of these patterns can start on an isolated point charge.
walkthrough: Identify the source: a single isolated positive point charge marked $+$ with spherically symmetric field around it.
State the rule: electric field lines show the force on a positive test charge, so a positive source repels the test charge outward.
Therefore the lines must be straight, radial, equally spaced in angle, and have arrowheads pointing away from the centre.
Diagrams A and B show concentric circular loops with tangential arrows. These never start or end on the charge and resemble a magnetic field, so reject them.
Diagram D shows radial lines but with arrows pointing inward, which is the pattern for a negative charge that attracts a positive test charge, so reject it.
Diagram C matches all requirements - radial straight lines with arrows outward. This is option C.
